Academic Advising Office (AAO) provides academic advising and support to the first and second year undergraduate students to ensure their successful academic progress. 

AAO Advisors are available to help students select and register for courses, assist students on transfer requirements and probation, provide peer support to students, and generally oversee the educational plan and student progress throughout their first year of studies. 
AAO responsibilities:  
Assist students in their consideration and clarification of course selection and academic requirements
Provide accurate information about University policies, procedures, and regulations
Assist students in evaluation or re-evaluation of academic progress toward established goals
Make referrals to resources within and outside of NU as appropriate

Student Support Fellowship (SSF) assists students with academic skills through tutoring sessions or receive advice from junior and senior students to help students grow academically and become a self-directed student. To learn more about the SSF please visit the AAO website at aao.nu.edu.kz. 

AAO Advisors are a reliable source of information about academic policies and extracurricular activities, and if you have any questions about the semester schedule, program curriculum, student progress or educational plan, please do not hesitate to contact us. 

Appointments 

Students are assigned to the AAO advisor prior to the start of their first semester at NU. Advising sessions are required for incoming first-year students to review the academic progress and educational plan, receive guidance towards the fulfillment of degree requirements and obtain information about campus resources. 

To schedule an appointment with AAO Advisors, please visit the AAO website at aao.nu.edu.kz
Find your academic advisor on the myRegistrar page, choose the relevant slots in Calendar of the advisor on the AAO website, and come to the meeting. 
To see the advisor, please come to Block 9, Rooms 9106, 9112 & 9113

Office Hours

Monday-Friday: 8:30 AM - 5:30 PM 

Contact information

Want to meet with the AAO advisor? Our advisors are here to help you! Contact AAO to request assistance or to make an appointment by:

Dropping by our office - Block 9, Rm. 9106, 9112 & 9113
Emailing our office at aao@nu.edu.kz. Advisors will either respond to you directly or refer your message to the appropriate office within 24-48 hours, Monday-Friday.
Using the AAO Website to see detailed information about AAO services: aao.nu.edu.kz
Keeping up with AAO social media to get the latest updates on AAO events & activities (AAO Instagram, Telegram Channel): 

○ AAO Instagram: @nu_aao 
○ AAO Telegram Channel: NU Academic Advising Office, @nu_aao

GPA provides students about their academic performance. A student who maintains a high GPA may be eligible to graduate with honors or to attend graduate school. 
Grade points are calculated by multiplying the number of credits by the numeric value of the grade for each course. The sum of the grade points is then divided by the total graded credits attempted. The total graded credits attempted, not the credits earned toward graduation, are used in computing the GPA.

The following is the example how GPA is calculated.

rows: CHEM 101 L General Chemistry I lab

blocks.text:
Enrolled Credits = 22, Earned Credits = 16 
Credit-Hour Value = 18.00 + 8.00 + 0 + 21.36 = 47.36 / 22 = 2.15 grade point average
Semester GPA: 2.15
The Cumulative GPA (CGPA) is computed by dividing the total cumulative grade points by the total graded credits attempted for courses taken in residence at NU.

Students are required to confirm a major by the end of their 1st year of studies.
To confirm a major in Business Administration, students should be in good academic standing and have completed the following courses with a grade of “C-” or above:

1. BUS 101 Core Course in Business 
2. ECON 101 Introduction to Microeconomics
3. MATH 161 Calculus I
4. ACCT 201 Introduction to Accounting

If a student fails to complete one course out of four with a grade of “C-” or above or withdraw from BUS 101, ECON 101, MATH 161 or ACCT 201 by the end of their 1st year, they are allowed to retake this course in the Fall term of the next academic year. Only one retake per course is allowed, including retake after withdrawal. In such a case, the student will remain with an unconfirmed major until the end of the Fall term of the 2nd academic year.

All courses must be passed with a grade of C- or better.

SCHOOL OF SCIENCES AND HUMANITIES
major confrimation requirements

All students of Sciences are accepted under their preferred major (Chemistry, Biological Sciences, Mathematics and Physics). After the progression audit at the end of the Spring students will be confirmed in their major. Students who don’t pass the progression audit will be given two options: to retake courses in summer or to become undeclared/change their major.

Students who choose Option 1 and successfully pass re-taken courses at the end of the summer term will be confirmed in their major. Students who choose Option 1 and again fail to meet the progression requirements will have the options of changing to a different major, to Undeclared, or withdraw/be dismissed from the University.
See major confirmation requirements on the next page.

blocks.text:
Declaring Social Data Science Minor Policy

The minor is open to students from all participating departments: Economics, Mathematics, Political Science, and Sociology. The number of students who can declare the minor is limited to 2 in each department for a total of 8. Two additional spots can be taken by more than two students within one department in case one department does not have any interested students.
The total number of students who can declare is 10 every year.
Students can apply for a Minor in Social Data Science at the end of the Fall of their 3rd year. The deadline to apply for a Minor in Social Data Science is at the end of the Fall of their 4th year.
